keyVerseText: Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb עֲוַל (ʻăval) is a primitive root word that conveys the fundamental idea of acting unjustly or wrongfully. Its core sense involves moral distortion or deviation from what is right, emphasizing a departure from integrity and righteousness. This root meaning enriches the English gloss 'deal unjustly' by highlighting an active, willful corruption of moral order rather than mere error or accident.
usageInScripture: The word עֲוַל appears only twice in the biblical text, consistently conveying the notion of unrighteous or unjust behavior. Its translations, such as 'of the unrighteous' and 'will he deal unjustly,' show a clear and stable semantic range centered on wrongful conduct. This consistency underscores the term's strong association with moral failure and cruelty, as seen in the contexts where it occurs.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֲוַל as deliberate moral distortion deepens our grasp of human sinfulness and the pervasive nature of unrighteousness that Scripture confronts. It reminds believers that sin is not merely a passive condition but an active deviation from God's justice and holiness. This awareness calls Christians to rely on God's deliverance and righteousness, recognizing that only He can rescue from the hands of those who act with such cruelty and injustice. The term thus highlights the necessity of divine intervention and grace in the face of human wrongdoing.
keyVerseReflection: In Psalms 71:4, the psalmist pleads, 'Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.' The use of עֲוַל here emphasizes the psalmist's peril at the hands of someone who actively deals unjustly, embodying moral corruption and cruelty. This word sharpens the urgency of the plea for God's rescue, portraying the adversary not just as an enemy but as one who willfully distorts justice, thus deepening the psalmist's dependence on God's righteous protection.
